properties.name: Road 3's hard part is ALREADY BUILT: release_seat fires from SeatLease's Drop, so the shared server observes a client disconnecting, crashing or being killed — and it deliberately writes nothing. Meanwhile a disciplined session ran 299 minutes between committed exports
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at main `8ba3198`, running the two experiments the user asked for against the store-inversion blockers.

═══ ROAD 3 IS NOT RESEARCH. THE OBSERVATION MECHANISM EXISTS AND RUNS TODAY. ═══

`dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` lists as its road 3: *"THE SERVER OWNS IT, NOT THE SESSION... the server is the only component that observes a session ENDING without being the session."* It is right, and the observing half is already written:

    identity.rs:625  impl Drop for SeatLease { fn drop(&mut self) { release_seat(&self.seat); } }

`release_seat`'s own doc: *"Called from the handler's Drop, so a client that disconnects, crashes or is killed releases its seat without having to say anything."* RAII, so it does not depend on an orderly shutdown or on any harness — which is precisely the objection that killed the Stop-hook answer (*"the guarantee cannot live in the harness, because the harness is the thing that might not come back"*).

The server also already knows HOW MANY are attached (`attached_seat_count`) and distinguishes three liveness states, refusing to guess for a seat it handed out but never leased (`Unknown`, never read as free).

🛑 **AND IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOTHING WITH IT.** `release_seat`'s doc continues: *"Nothing is written to the graph — the CLAIM stays exactly where it was, and only its liveness changes."* ⇒ **The gap between what exists and road 3 is not detection. It is one action on an event that already fires.**

⚠️ BOUND: `Drop` does not run if the SERVER ITSELF is SIGKILLed. That is a strictly smaller exposure than today's, because the server outliving any one session is the premise of the road, and session death is far commoner than daemon death. It is not zero, and a periodic export (road 2) is what would cover it.

═══ THE EXPOSURE, MEASURED ON A SESSION THAT WAS TRYING ═══

Five exporting commits across 562 minutes of one working session, taken from git:

    gaps between committed exports:  36 min | 186 min | 299 min | 41 min
    longest window with the durable copy stale:  299 MINUTES (~5 HOURS)
    design delta over the session:  +15 nodes, +37 edges, ~10 property-only edits

⭐⭐ **THIS IS THE NUMBER THE BLOCKER NEEDED, AND IT IS NOT A NEGLIGENCE NUMBER.** The session exported at every PR boundary, ran the design gate each time, and was actively disciplined about the export-once-per-PR rule. It STILL spent five unbroken hours with the committed document behind the live graph. Under today's model that costs a session's work; under the inversion the same five hours is THE DESIGN.

📌 AND THE KNOB IS ESSENTIALLY FREE. Save is measured at **265 ms** (`dec:the-rust-rocksdb-switch-is-parked-until-the-store-question-settles`). A debounced or on-idle export at any cadence a person would notice costs a quarter of a second against a five-hour window. **The trade is not cost against safety; it is 265 ms against five hours.**

⚠️ BOUNDS: one session, one machine, one person, one design. Gaps are between COMMITTED exports — the working tree was written more often than that, so this measures the durable-copy exposure rather than every write.
